name: taghairm

attributes.attribute: Scottish divination rite that roasted live cats
the Irish name for the king of cats

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Taghairm was a rite of divination used in Scotland. Old texts say that conjurers roasted live cats over a fire. The heat called up a giant cat. The story names this beast Big-Ears. The cat may come from an older tale of the king of cats, known in Ireland as Irusan. The rite lived on into the seventeenth century. The clergy preached against it. They said that any user was bound for hell.

okr.objective: Record taghairm as a Scottish ritual of divination.
key_results: Describes the rite of roasting live cats to summon a great beast
Links the beast to the Irish king of cats Irusan
Notes that clergy said its users were damned
